message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most iconic and widely celebrated sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (completed in 1889). **Why it’s considered the most famous:** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin – a leading figure of French sculpture who bridged Romanticism and modernism. | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) – firmly within the 19th century. | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist approach with expressive, almost unfinished surfaces that capture intimate human emotion. | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became an emblem of romantic love and sensuality.
• Inspired countless reproductions, parodies, and references in literature, film, and popular culture.
• Its dramatic pose and tactile surface set a new standard for how sculpture could convey psychological depth. | | **Legacy** | • Frequently cited as a turning point toward modern sculpture.
• Continues to be displayed in major museums worldwide (e.g., Musée Rodin in Paris, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York). | **Other notable 19th‑century sculptures that rival its fame:** | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | “The Gates of Hell” | Auguste Rodin | 1880–1908 (unfinished) | A monumental, complex work that influenced modern art and architecture. | | “The Thinker” | Auguste Rodin | 1902–1904 (early 20th century) | Though technically early 20th, it’s often associated with Rodin’s 19th‑century legacy. | | “The Birth of Venus” (modern reinterpretation) | Various artists | 19th‑century reinterpretations | Revived interest in classical themes with contemporary techniques. | **Bottom line:** While several masterpieces emerged during the 19th century, Rodin’s “The Kiss” stands out as the most universally recognized and celebrated sculpture from that era.
